qt: to the Commission Marcin Sypniewski (ESN) Subject:

In many sectors, particularly in the drinks industry, schemes for the reuse of glass bottles, crates, kegs and other packaging have been in operation for years. However, businesses are warning of uncertainty regarding the application of the new PPWR requirements to packaging already in circulation and the method for recording the number of times it has been reused. Individually marking and tracking millions of items of packaging could require costly technical changes, while withdrawing packaging that is still usable would lead to the generation of additional waste. In light of the above: 1.

Will the Commission confirm that reusable packaging placed on the market before the new labelling requirements enter into force may remain in circulation until the end of its natural life without the need for modernisation?

Can compliance with the requirements regarding the number of circulation cycles be demonstrated on the basis of reliable statistical and operational data, without the need to track each item of packaging individually?
Will existing reuse schemes be deemed compliant with the PPWR without the need to redraft documentation and demonstrate compliance with Annex VI?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (29.10.2026) The labelling requirements under the Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR)1 for all packaging, including reusable packaging, will apply 24 months from the date of entry into force of the implementing act setting out the labelling specifications. This act is currently under preparation. Reusable packaging placed on the market before the new labelling requirements apply may remain in circulation and would not need to be redesigned solely to meet the new requirements. Regarding the number of rotations, the future Implementing act on labelling, adopted pursuant to Article 12(1), will guide operators on which data are needed to calculate the number of rotations and the method to be used. The PPWR expressly recognises existing re-use systems as a means of complying with the requirements applicable to re-use systems. Existing re-use systems may therefore continue to be used, provided that they meet the applicable requirements of Article 26 and Annex VI.
1 Regulation (EU) 2025/40 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 19 December 2024 on packaging
and packaging waste, amending Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 and Directive (EU) 2019/904, and repealing Directive 94/62/EC, OJ L, 2025/40, 22.1.2025.
